PR158_FINDING_1_RESOLUTION

The mandatory fresh ordinary-ChatGPT review reported one P2 finding against the previous head 3bafac44c9548be667dfbb22f9b171b9012bfef0.

Disposition: CONFIRMED.

Problem:
- ROADMAP.md declared vendor/research project names non-roadmap stages;
- the same authoritative ROADMAP still retained a named `Pre-26.4 — bounded OpenAdapt integration spike` stage.

Fix on current head 884b6fbf9af135f6bb36fe923122d5526e1c4dd7:
- renamed/reframed the section as `Pre-26.4 — bounded external-procedure integration qualification`;
- made the target flow vendor-neutral;
- explicitly states OpenAdapt is only one previously researched candidate and may be selected, adapted or rejected by fresh Stage Research;
- preserved project-owned Verification Kernel / Finish Gate boundaries and ADOPT/ADAPT/REJECT exit semantics.

A full ROADMAP scan found no second vendor-named roadmap stage. UFO/UFO² remains only an implementation candidate inside the generic 26.5 Hybrid Computer-Use Integration stage.

Because this is a material roadmap/process correction, the previous review is stale. A fresh ordinary-ChatGPT review is required for:

HEAD_SHA=884b6fbf9af135f6bb36fe923122d5526e1c4dd7

PR158_FINDING_2_RESOLUTION

Mandatory fresh ordinary-ChatGPT review on previous head 884b6fbf9af135f6bb36fe923122d5526e1c4dd7 reported one P2 finding.

Disposition: CONFIRMED -> GUARDED.

Finding:
The previous vendor-specific roadmap-stage defect was corrected in prose, but BASE policy AGENTS.md §2A requires confirmed material findings to be closed by failure class with the strongest practical executable guard. Existing documentation consistency tests had allowed the original `Pre-26.4 — bounded OpenAdapt integration spike` to remain green.

Root cause:
`test_release_order_has_one_authoritative_owner` verified ownership/order but did not constrain roadmap stage headings from promoting known research/vendor candidates into the authoritative release sequence.

Failure class:
A research/vendor implementation candidate is placed in a Markdown heading that functions as an authoritative roadmap stage, silently converting an optional candidate into required-looking release work.

Repository-wide search:
The current ROADMAP has 25 Markdown headings. No current heading contains the known research/vendor candidate names guarded below. Candidate mentions in explanatory body text remain allowed and are explicitly subordinate to fresh Stage Research.

Guard added on current head 4d1e9cd38930899cbc49abad8b363d8ceaddb5f6:
`tests/test_documentation_consistency.py::test_authoritative_roadmap_stage_headings_do_not_promote_research_candidates`

The guard extracts all Markdown headings from authoritative ROADMAP.md and rejects known candidate names:
- OpenAdapt
- Prime
- CCCC
- AREX
- Skill Recorder
- WinApp
- UFO
- Coddy

It intentionally does not ban these names from body text, where they may remain research candidates subject to ADOPT/ADAPT/REJECT.

Because this adds executable acceptance coverage, the previous review is stale. Fresh exact-head review is required for:
BASE_SHA=92ef431b9d412bd78307c51641b1379184fe560d
HEAD_SHA=4d1e9cd38930899cbc49abad8b363d8ceaddb5f6

PR158_FINDING_3_RESOLUTION

Mandatory fresh ordinary-ChatGPT review on previous head 3afe224220e8d07a4024c5539e0bcf879efe4822 reported one P2 finding.

Disposition: CONFIRMED -> GUARDED.

Finding:
The strengthened roadmap guard still filtered detailed headings by a finite list of recognized prefixes. A new top-level release-looking heading with an unrecognized prefix (for example `Pre-26.5 — OpenAdapt integration qualification`) could reproduce the confirmed failure class while remaining invisible to the guard.

Root cause:
The regression guard was selective instead of exhaustive: it validated only headings it first chose to recognize.

Failure class:
Any new authoritative-looking level-1 ROADMAP section can silently enter the release document if the guard excludes it before validation.

Repository-wide search:
ROADMAP.md currently contains 16 level-1 headings. The active release/research structure is fully enumerable and no current unclassified level-1 heading exists.

Guard on current head aaaf2d52965a0dbcc7a1f0805f383cbe0da06464:
`tests/test_documentation_consistency.py::test_authoritative_roadmap_stages_are_capability_owned`

The guard now:
- still pins the canonical eight-item capability-owned release sequence;
- extracts every level-1 Markdown heading in ROADMAP.md;
- asserts the complete ordered tuple of all 16 level-1 headings;
- therefore any new top-level heading, regardless of prefix/vendor name, fails CI until explicitly classified by updating the guard.

This intentionally makes top-level ROADMAP structure review-sensitive. Lower-level explanatory headings/body text remain free to evolve without this exact tuple.

Because the guard changed materially, the previous review is stale. Fresh exact-head review is required for:
BASE_SHA=92ef431b9d412bd78307c51641b1379184fe560d
HEAD_SHA=aaaf2d52965a0dbcc7a1f0805f383cbe0da06464

PR158_FINDING_4_RESOLUTION

Mandatory fresh ordinary-ChatGPT review on previous head aaaf2d52965a0dbcc7a1f0805f383cbe0da06464 reported one P2 finding.

Disposition: CONFIRMED -> GUARDED.

Finding:
The V5 guard claimed exhaustive level-1 ROADMAP coverage but parsed only ATX `# ...` headings. A valid Setext H1 (title + `====`) could reproduce the confirmed stage-promotion failure class while remaining invisible. The raw regex could also falsely count `# ...` inside fenced code as a real heading.

Root cause:
The guard tried to approximate all Markdown H1 semantics with one raw ATX regex.

Failure class:
Alternate top-level heading syntax or heading-looking content inside code fences can bypass or falsely trigger the authoritative ROADMAP structure guard.

Selected closure:
Do not build a full Markdown parser. Standardize authoritative ROADMAP top-level sections on one project-owned syntax: ATX H1 (`# ...`) outside fenced code.

Guard on current head 0aa09e5defc28cec4256c108df5394cb5e5aceb6:
- `_roadmap_top_level_structure()` is fence-aware for backtick and tilde fenced code;
- ATX H1 outside fences is collected;
- Setext H1 underline syntax (`====`) outside fences is rejected;
- raw HTML `<h1>` outside fences is rejected;
- unterminated fenced code is rejected;
- the complete ordered ATX H1 tuple remains pinned;
- adversarial fixtures prove Setext bypass is rejected and heading-like content inside fenced code is ignored.

This closes the reported bypass without claiming a complete Markdown parser.

Because the guard changed materially, the previous review is stale. Fresh exact-head review is required for:
BASE_SHA=92ef431b9d412bd78307c51641b1379184fe560d
HEAD_SHA=0aa09e5defc28cec4256c108df5394cb5e5aceb6

pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Turn the current release plan into a product-outcome roadmap and make PR #151 explicitly subordinate research/idea-bank material.

## Product decisions recorded

- `ROADMAP.md` owns the concrete CAP v1 implementation sequence.
- Named projects such as Prime, CCCC, AREX, Skill Recorder, WinApp CLI and OpenAdapt are research/reuse candidates, not mandatory roadmap stages.
- Immediate development work becomes automatic-reviewer migration onto the accepted generic Delegation lifecycle.
- The concrete `chatgpt-temporary` adapter is reviewer-only product infrastructure.
- Ordinary CAP tasks remain in the user's ordinary ChatGPT conversation through the accepted six-tool semantic route.
- The earlier non-reviewer Temporary Chat qualification remains evidence that generic Delegation was not reviewer-specific; it does not authorize Temporary Chat as a normal task mode.
- Future non-reviewer isolated-worker use requires fresh Stage Research rather than silently widening `chatgpt-temporary`.

## Product sequence

1. reviewer reuse over accepted Delegation lifecycle;
2. broad real-application computer-use coverage;
3. external procedure integration;
4. skill lifecycle;
5. skill acquisition;
6. hybrid capability use;
7. distribution;
8. clean-user stable release.

## #151

PR #151 has been relabeled in its own description as **RESEARCH / IDEA BANK — NOT THE PRODUCT ROADMAP**. Its research remains available for later re-entry but no longer reads as the project's immediate implementation queue.

## Scope

Documentation/process direction only. No runtime, dependency, public tool, authority implementation or production behavior changes in this PR.

Because this changes release-order/process direction, keep this PR Draft until exact-head documentation/contract checks and the repository's applicable review policy are satisfied.
## Semantic surface evolution

The six-tool surface remains the current accepted contract, not a permanent magic number. `procedure_run` remains a closed registered-procedure surface and must not become a generic dispatcher. New skills normally compose existing capabilities; a new top-level tool is considered only for a genuinely new planner-visible interactive consequence class with separate acceptance.
